attempts.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Medieval Georgian-Persian illuminated manuscript miniature painting for Shota Rustaveli's "The Knight in the Panther's Skin" (ვეფხისტყაოსანი). 16th–17th-century Georgian royal manuscript miniature, Mamuka Tavakarashvili / King Vakhtang VI illumination tradition blended with classical Persian-Safavid tempera miniature. Egg tempera, lapis lazuli, malachite green, vermilion, warm ochre and burnished antique gold leaf on aged ivory-parchment vellum. Stylized faceted rocky cliffs, ornamental cypress and pomegranate trees, intricately patterned arches and domes, expressive courtly figures in medieval Georgian-Eastern attire. Fine controlled contours, delicately patterned fabrics, luminous matte mineral pigments, slightly flattened layered miniature space with expressive narrative gestures. A painted manuscript scene, not photorealism, cinematic rendering, modern digital fantasy or a collage of circular portraits. Reuse referenced character faces and coloring but adapt costume to the actual chronological story scene; Tariel wears ordinary Indian court or military attire in early backstory, his panther skin belongs to his later exile. Exact horizontal 16:10 composition, preferably native 1600x1000 pixels, a single coherent scene framed for a card vignette. Soft natural painted vignette dissolving to warm aged ivory vellum at edges, modest antique-gold floral flourishes at the perimeter, no rigid border. Key faces and gestures comfortably inside the central safe area, no important content cut off. STRICTLY NO TEXT, NO LETTERS, NO CAPTIONS, NO NUMBERS, NO INSCRIPTIONS, NO CALLIGRAPHY, NO BANNERS, NO SCROLLS, NO SIGNATURES, NO WATERMARKS anywhere. Architectural ornament must be purely floral/geometric with no pseudo-writing. If letters are narratively necessary, use a small closed plain unmarked folded paper or sealed envelope, never visible writing or rolled scrolls. All book covers/pages must be plain and unmarked. Do not show graphic blood or gore; imply violent events through gestures, context and intact clothing.
Episode 06: Tariel's Upbringing in India & First Sight of Nestan.
Selected remembered scene in India: the secluded garden pavilion of Nestan-Darejan inside King Parsadan's palace. Asmat gently draws aside a patterned vermilion-and-gold curtain, revealing Nestan poised in a luminous emerald-green court dress embroidered with antique gold, a small emerald-and-gold circlet and long dark curls beneath a delicate dark veil. Her noble youthful face matches the Nestan reference. Young adult Tariel, arriving from a hunt beside King Parsadan, is overwhelmed at this first sight: he staggers with one hand to his heart and his knees slightly weakening, his gaze fixed upon Nestan. Parsadan reaches a steadying hand to his upper arm. Tariel's short dark beard, expressive eyes and wavy dark hair match his portrait, but his costume is appropriate to the Indian past: elegant lapis-blue-and-gold court/hunting tunic, leather belt, boots, no fur. Bareheaded dark curls or a plain blue court cap. King Parsadan has medium-length wavy grey hair, neatly shaped grey beard, a low ruby-and-gold crown and burgundy robes with gold vine embroidery. Asmat has a simple charcoal-black hooded dress, gold edging and serious gentle face. Four physically co-present principal figures: Tariel, Nestan, Asmat and Parsadan.
Architecture: airy Georgian-Eastern garden pavilion, intricate floral arches, lapis mosaic domes, pomegranate boughs, cypress and a modest fountain. Slightly flattened narrative miniature space with expressive gestures, clear distance and connection between Tariel and the revealed princess.
Historical constraints: this is the remembered Indian court BEFORE Tariel's exile. Absolutely no panther-skin mantle, striped fur hat or tiger pelt on Tariel. Saridan has already died: do not add him. No Avtandil, no cave-narration frame. No extra Davar in this selected moment.
References: image1 is STYLE ONLY. Images2–5 identify Tariel, Nestan, Asmat and Parsadan respectively. Follow faces and color identities while changing Tariel's costume as explicitly stated; do not copy circular medallion borders. Horizontal16:10, approximately1600x1000 native pixels, soft painted ivory vignette and small gold floral perimeter flourishes. STRICTLY NO TEXT, LETTERS, NUMBERS, CALLIGRAPHY, BANNERS OR SCROLLS anywhere.

visual_qa.scene: Asmat reveals Nestan at her Indian pavilion; Tariel staggers in overwhelming first love while Parsadan steadies him.
visual_qa.early_tariel_costume: Blue/gold court tunic, no panther pelt; Saridan and Avtandil absent.
